title: India adverse event reporting: when a serious adverse event report is owed, and by when
plain: A serious adverse event suspected to be associated with the device: report within 15 calendar days (India MDR 2017 Rule 26(ii), "within fifteen days"); the awareness day is day 1. The organization's India window is used only when it is exactly 15 calendar days.
law_in_force_from: Medical Devices Rules 2017 (in force 1 January 2018) (for your consultant to confirm)

change.reason: B9 (FG-2): version 1 held no legal period for India and took the organization's window, any length. Version 2 adds the 15 calendar days of Rule 26(ii). A correction of MDARIX's own rule, not a law change: same period as version 1 (from the start). Signed conclusions keep version 1 and their due date; unsigned drafts are saved again.

review.note: Starter, for your consultant to confirm.

approval.note: B9 spec approved 11 Nov 2026 (B9-D1): 15 calendar days, awareness day = day 1, a correction from the start.

question_set.title: India adverse event reporting (Medical Devices Rules 2017)

questions.text: Is it an adverse event suspected to be associated with the device?
questions.definition: An adverse event: an untoward occurrence in a patient, user or other person where the device is suspected to have caused or contributed to it.

questions.text: Serious, criterion (a): did it result in death?
questions.definition: A serious adverse event (India MDR 2017, starter text: criteria to confirm against the Rules and the MDAE form) results in death, is life-threatening, needs in-patient hospitalisation or prolongs it, results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, is a congenital anomaly or birth defect, or needs an intervention to prevent permanent impairment or damage. Answer each criterion on its own.

Unexpected: its nature or severity is not consistent with the device's labelling or the risks known for it. A serious and unexpected event is a suspected unexpected serious adverse event.
